wow: Photograph a bottle from your shelf; the page overlays every INCI line with its read text and '1.1 mm' tags, turns the 0.9 mm line red, and flags 'Paraden' as a typo against the approved artwork PDF.
train_what: GLM-OCR 0.9B (mlx-vlm LoRA) outputting structured JSON: lines, bbox, estimated font height in mm, curvature; MoGe-3 used frozen for metric scale
data_plan: Blender renders of the 20 own bottle models with labels typeset from real ingredient vocabularies (EU CosIng public INCI list, Korean 전성분 phrasing) in random fonts, sizes 0.8-3 mm, on cylinders and tubes, glossy and matte, with glare and phone noise: 8,000 images at 1024 with exact per-line text, bbox and physical mm height known from the scene scale. 100 real iPhone photos of own bottles with a ruler in frame as validation for the mm estimate.
mac_plan: Render ~3 h. mlx-vlm LoRA on GLM-OCR 0.9B, ~6 GB, 1.5 h. Runtime on Mac: MoGe-3 on MLX gives metric point map -> px/mm along the label surface; OCR LoRA reads lines; a small Python diff (rapidfuzz) compares to the artwork text extracted by GLM-OCR from the PDF. ~2 s per photo end to end.
demo: Local web tool inside beu: photo in, annotated overlay, JSON report, artwork-diff table with configurable minimum-size thresholds per regulation.
risk: MoGe metric scale error 5-10 percent on close-ups; glare wipes out text on glossy labels. Report confidence per line and require two photos for sub-1 mm claims.
uses: SAM 3 / SAM 3.1 text-prompted segmentation (browser INT8 ONNX + MLX)

title: Taste Judge
one_liner: A reward model of the user's own packaging taste, trained from two hours of swiping on generated bottle variants, then used as the fitness function for an overnight evolutionary loop of label designs.
wow: A timeline of 20 generations of bottles converging on 'what this person likes' with no prompt ever describing it; visitors upload their own design and the judge scores it against the user's taste and against the base model's average taste, with a one-sentence critique.
train_what: UnifiedReward-Flex-qwen3vl-4b (LoRA via mlx-vlm, pairwise Bradley-Terry loss); fallback Qwen3.5-2B VLM
data_plan: Population of 3,000 packaging variants: Boogu-Image-0.1 Turbo label designs, Ideogram-4 typographic labels and Blender renders of the own 20 bottles with random palettes/materials (reusing the Material Dial renderer). A local swipe page in the beu frontend serves random pairs; at ~5 s per choice the user labels 1,500 pairs in ~2 h across two evenings; 200 pairs held out. CapRL-Qwen3VL-2B captions supply the critique text for a small SFT mix so the judge explains its score.
mac_plan: Generation: Boogu/Ideogram/Z-Image-Turbo ~4-8 s each, ~4 h for 3,000 images. mlx-vlm LoRA on the 4B judge, ~10 GB, ~1 h; eval agreement on held-out pairs vs zero-shot UnifiedReward. Evolution loop: Z-Image-Turbo img2img mutations + Qwen-Image-Edit color/material mutations, 200 candidates per generation, judge ranks, 20 generations overnight (~8 h).
demo: Blog page: generation timeline strip, 'taste divergence' chart (own judge vs base judge), upload-and-score widget backed by a local server or precomputed examples.
risk: 1,500 pairs may only learn palette preference; overfit shows as low held-out agreement (<70 percent). Mitigate with pair sampling stratified by material/typography and an ablation reporting agreement per attribute.

title: Favorites Model — a reward model of your own eye
one_liner: Train a personal aesthetic reward model from the two label sources you already own (Apple Photos favorites vs. everything else, plus a two-hour swipe session over your own Z-Image/Klein generations) and ship it as a 90 MB in-browser scorer that says how much *you* would like any image.
wow: A visitor drops 20 photos into the page and watches them re-sort in real time by 'Changkeun-likeness', with a heat overlay (Grad-CAM on DINOv3 patch tokens) showing which region drove the score. Next to it, your entire camera roll (12k thumbnails) ordered by the model, favorites highlighted — and the ones it thinks you should have favorited but didn't.
train_what: Two students of one preference set: (a) browser-size — frozen DINOv3 ViT-S/16 (onnx-community) + a 2-layer Bradley-Terry head trained in MLX; (b) Mac-size, explainable — LoRA on UnifiedReward-Flex-qwen3vl-4b so it outputs a score AND a one-sentence Korean reason in your vocabulary.
data_plan: Source 1 (zero labeling): export Apple Photos via osxphotos — ~12k photos, ~600 favorited → weak positives; hard negatives = photos taken within 10 s of a favorite but not favorited (near-duplicate pairs isolate taste, not subject). ~5k pairs. Source 2: generate 1,500 images with Z-Image-Turbo/Klein from 150 blog/beu-style prompts (~2 h), then a swipe UI (left/right + optional 3-word reason) at ~3 s per pair → 2,000 explicit pairs in two evenings. Reasons become the text targets for the 4B judge. Held-out: 300 pairs, and 200 pairs your partner/friend labels to measure that the model tracks YOU, not generic aesthetics (agreement gap is the headline number).
mac_plan: DINOv3-S embeddings for 13.5k images: ~10 min (ONNX Runtime CoreML EP or MLX port). BT head: seconds; run 50 seeds and report agreement variance. UnifiedReward-Flex 4B LoRA via mlx-vlm (r=16, 2 epochs over 2k pairs+reasons, 768px): ~9 GB weights, peak ~25 GB, ~1.5 h. Browser export: DINOv3-S ONNX q8 (~22 MB) + head, WebGPU. Total ≈ 1 weekend.
demo: Blog page: drag-and-drop ranking with Grad-CAM heat, the camera-roll wall sorted by taste, and a scoreboard: held-out agreement (self) vs. agreement with another person vs. LAION-aesthetic baseline. This model is the artifact the next concept (Taste-GRPO) consumes.
risk: Favorites in Photos may encode 'people I love' more than 'images I like'; the near-duplicate pairing mitigates but does not remove it. UnifiedReward-Flex LoRA in mlx-vlm may need the model added to mlx-vlm's registry (Qwen3-VL family is supported, but verify the checkpoint loads).

title: Taste-GRPO — the generator that learns to please one person
one_liner: Run a closed RL loop on your Mac: Klein 4B (or Z-Image-Turbo) generates 8 candidates per prompt, the Favorites Model scores them, a Diffusion-DPO/RAFT LoRA update follows, repeat for 5 rounds — the model drifts toward your taste with no human in the loop after round 0.
wow: A 'generation timeline' grid: same 12 prompts × same seeds, columns are RL rounds 0→5, and you can visibly see the drift (your recurring preferences — one colour, hard shadow, negative space — emerge without ever being written in a prompt). Below it a blind A/B where visitors pick round-0 vs round-5; the page counts how often strangers agree with your reward model.
train_what: LoRA (r=32, attention+MLP) on FLUX.2 Klein 4B in mflux, with the mflux LoRA trainer's loss replaced by Diffusion-DPO (winner/loser pair, frozen reference = base) — fallback to RAFT (reward-ranked fine-tuning: plain LoRA on top-2 of 8). Reward = Favorites Model (concept 1) mixed 0.7/0.3 with UnifiedReward prompt-alignment so it cannot collapse into 'orange blur'.
data_plan: Fully synthetic and self-generated: 200 prompts mined from your blog posts + beu briefs (Qwen3.5-9B rewrites them into 200 short image prompts). Per round: 200 prompts × 8 samples × 4 steps at 768px = 1,600 images (~1.2 h), scored in ~2 min, → 400 DPO pairs (top vs bottom per prompt). 5 rounds = 8k generated images, 2k pairs. Round-0 human check: you swipe 100 pairs to confirm reward sign; if agreement <75% stop and retrain concept 1.
mac_plan: Klein 4B bf16 (~8 GB) + Qwen3 text encoder (~8 GB) + reference copy for DPO (+8 GB) + activations at 768px ≈ 45 GB peak — comfortable on 128 GB. DPO LoRA step at 512–768px ≈ 4 s; 400 pairs × 3 epochs ≈ 1.5 h per round; sampling 1.2 h per round → ~3 h/round, 5 rounds ≈ 15 h = one weekend running unattended via a Makefile target. Tooling: mflux (Klein LoRA training verified), MLX for reward, a 150-line DPO loss patch.
demo: Blog page with the timeline grid, a reward-curve chart per round (mean reward, KL-to-base proxy = LPIPS drift), the blind A/B with a live agreement counter (artifact db), and the final LoRA on HF. Plus a 40-second video of round transitions with the same seed.
risk: Reward hacking is the real content here — document it. Diffusion-DPO in mflux requires you to run two forward passes per pair; if mflux's trainer is too rigid, RAFT gives 70% of the effect with zero loss surgery. Klein is distilled/few-step, which makes DPO gradients noisier; Z-Image-Turbo 6B is the alternate base.

title: 5 MB Hero — a from-scratch ternary one-step generator living in the blog header
one_liner: Extend your minrf-web experiment into a full craft piece: train a 30M-param rectified-flow DiT from scratch on one narrow domain of your own (the Formless 3D typography renders + your city-walk photos), distill it to ONE step with MeanFlow, quantize to ternary with BitNet-style QAT, and ship it as a ~6 MB WebGPU model that generates a fresh hero image every page load in <50 ms.
wow: Every visitor to blog.beu-labs.com gets a never-before-seen image generated in their own tab before the fonts finish loading, and a small badge reads '30M params · 1 step · 1.58 bit · 6.1 MB'. A slider lets them scrub steps 1→8 and bits fp16→ternary to see exactly what the compression cost.
train_what: From scratch: pixel-space 128×128 DiT-S-ish (12 blocks, width 384, ~30M params), rectified flow → MeanFlow one-step objective (fine-tune from the RF weights) → BitNet b1.58 QAT (ternary weights, 8-bit activations, absmean scaling) for the last 20% of steps → ONNX/WebGPU with packed 2-bit weights unpacked in a shader.
data_plan: Own data, two domains to pick from: (A) 20k renders of the Formless cover (your existing LivingTitle/ogl scene) with randomized camera, light, colour and layer-count — rendered headless via Playwright in ~1 h, so the dataset is *your own generative code* as teacher; (B) 6k of your city-walk/desk photos, centre-cropped, plus 10k Z-Image-Turbo 512px synthetic in the same style (~6 s each, 17 h overnight). Domain (A) needs no diffusion model at all, which is the purer story. Held-out FID/KID against 1k reserved renders per checkpoint.
mac_plan: MLX, batch 128 at 128px: ~3.5 it/s on M4 Max → 100k RF steps ≈ 8 h (memory <10 GB). MeanFlow distillation 20k steps ≈ 2 h. Ternary QAT 20k steps ≈ 2 h. Export via mlx→safetensors→custom ONNX or hand-written WGSL matmul (onnxruntime-web has no ternary kernels; a 2-bit unpack shader is ~80 lines). Total ≈ 1.5 weekends; the RF training runs overnight.
demo: The blog hero itself, plus a lab page with the steps/bits scrub, FID table per (steps × bits), and a timeline of training checkpoints as a filmstrip. Model weights on HF with the WGSL kernel.
risk: Ternary QAT on a 30M model can lose fine structure at 128px; the fallback is 4-bit (still ~15 MB). Safari 26 WebGPU compute-shader limits (workgroup size, storage buffer size) must be checked early. Pixel-space at 128px caps resolution — pair with Swin2SR in-browser 2× if you want 256px.
sources: https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/bonsai-image-ternary-4B-mlx-2bit (ternary diffusion exists — proof it holds up)
uses: SeedVR2-3B one-step restoration (MLX) + Swin2SR in browser

title: Critic in My Voice — a 2B VLM judge fine-tuned on your packaging standards
one_liner: Fine-tune Qwen3.5-2B VLM to critique cosmetic-packaging renders exactly the way you do (Korean, your criteria: label hierarchy, cap-to-body ratio, finish coherence, shelf readability) and run it on-device in beu so every design gets your review even when you are asleep.
wow: In beu, a visitor drops a bottle render and within 4 s gets a 5-line Korean critique with a score out of 10 and a pointed fix — generated in their browser. A side-by-side shows the base model's generic 'the design is clean and modern' versus your fine-tuned one saying '캡 비율이 몸통 대비 과해서 셀프 존 20cm 거리에서 로고가 죽는다'. The page also reports: on 150 held-out pairs, the judge picks the same design as you 84% of the time; base model 58%.
train_what: LoRA (r=16, all linear) on Qwen3.5-2B (native-multimodal) via mlx-vlm; two output formats trained jointly: free-text critique and a pairwise JSON verdict {winner, score_a, score_b, reason}. Second export: merged weights → ONNX q4f16 following onnx-community's Qwen3.5-2B-ONNX-OPT conversion for Transformers.js.
data_plan: Seed: you write 150 critiques (2 evenings, ~4 min each) on beu renders + Boogu-Image/Ideogram-4 generated packaging (600 images generated locally in ~2 h). Expansion by a local teacher: Qwen3.5-27B (4-bit, MLX) or Gemma-4 27B rewrites/extends to 3,000 critiques conditioned on your 150 as style exemplars + a rubric you wrote; CapRL-2B adds factual captions so critiques stay grounded. Pairwise set: 1,200 pairs where you pick a winner in a swipe UI (~1 h). You audit 300 synthetic samples; anything rejected is a hard negative for a second pass. Held-out: 150 pairs + 50 critiques rated blind by you (yours vs. model's).
mac_plan: Qwen3.5-2B bf16 ≈ 4.5 GB; LoRA at 768px images, batch 4, 3 epochs over 4.2k samples ≈ 1.5–2 h on M4 Max (peak ~20 GB). Teacher expansion with a 27B 4-bit model at ~25 tok/s: 3k critiques × 150 tokens ≈ 5 h unattended. ONNX export + WebGPU validation: half a day. Total ≈ 1 weekend + 2 evenings of writing.
demo: beu page with the on-device critic (q4f16, ~1.4 GB click-to-load) and the agreement scoreboard; a 'critique diff' view base vs. yours on the same image; the rubric + 150 seed critiques released as a small dataset.
risk: ONNX re-export after LoRA merge is the fragile step (custom vision-tower export scripts); fallback is serving from your Mac via mlx-vlm with the browser demo pointed at it. Teacher-expanded data can flatten your voice — keep the human-written 150 upweighted 5× in the loss.

title: One Photo, One Network — distilling a 20B relighter into a 2 MB shader of your desk
one_liner: Take one photo of your desk (or apartment corner), have Qwen-Image-Edit + Relight LoRA produce 400 relit versions under sampled light directions, then distill them into a tiny per-photo neural light field that you bake into a GLSL fragment shader in ogl — the artwork is a 2 MB network that only knows how light moves across your desk.
wow: On the blog, the desk photo follows the visitor's cursor: drag left and the window light swings, shadows of the monitor and the plant slide correctly, the mug's specular moves — at 60 fps, no server, no 3D asset. A toggle shows the raw teacher frames vs. the student, and the size badge: 'teacher 20B · student 1.9M params · 2.1 MB'.
train_what: Distillation from Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 (+ dx8152 Relight LoRA, Lightning 4-step) into a per-image conditional network: input = (u, v, MoGe-3 normal, depth, albedo from Marigold-IID, light direction θ,φ, intensity), output = RGB; architecture = 8-layer SIREN/MLP with hash-grid features (~1.9M params). Trained in MLX; weights exported as float16 textures and evaluated in a fragment shader.
data_plan: Your own photo (1 image, 1536px). Teacher renders: 400 variants over a hemisphere of light directions × 3 intensities, plus 40 'colour temperature' variants — Relight LoRA instruction templates ('light from upper-left window, warm, hard shadows'), 4 steps at 1024px ≈ 25 s each ≈ 3 h overnight. Filter: reject frames where DINOv3 similarity to the source drops below a threshold (geometry hallucinated). Intrinsics (normals/depth/albedo) come from MoGe-3 and Marigold-IID, run once. Held-out: 40 light directions never seen in training; report PSNR/LPIPS of student vs. teacher on them.
mac_plan: Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 4-bit via mflux ≈ 14 GB + Relight LoRA; 440 edits ≈ 3 h unattended. MoGe-3 + Marigold-IID: 10 min. Student training in MLX: 440 frames × 1536² pixels sampled at 64k rays/step, 30k steps ≈ 1 h (<6 GB). Shader baking: an afternoon in ogl (weights as RGBA16F textures, matmul in the fragment shader). Total ≈ 1 weekend.
demo: Blog hero/section with cursor-driven light, a teacher-vs-student toggle, the held-out PSNR chart, and a second instance on a beu bottle packshot. The 2 MB weight texture and shader on GitHub.
risk: The teacher is not physically consistent across frames (shadows may jitter between samples); the student smooths this, which is often a feature but can blur hard shadows — add a light-direction-conditioned shadow map from the MoGe depth as an explicit input if it does. Relight LoRA was trained for 2509; verify it loads on 2511 in mflux (fall back to IC-Light via ONNX as teacher).

title: Edit ⇄ Undo — a self-play data engine that teaches a 4B editor your objects and your Korean
one_liner: Build a closed data engine with no human labels: a 20B teacher edits your desk/plant/apartment photos, then undoes its own edit; only cycle-consistent, judge-approved triples survive, and those train a Klein 4B edit LoRA that understands Korean instructions about YOUR objects ('몬스테라 화분을 왼쪽 창가로') — the engine's filter stats are as much the artifact as the model.
wow: A live 'data engine dashboard' on the blog: 2,400 candidate edits flowing through three gates (cycle-consistency, VLM judge, dedup) with pass rates, and a gallery where visitors type a Korean instruction on your actual desk photo and see the 4B student's result next to the 20B teacher's — the student is 5× smaller and runs in 6 s on your Mac. Hovering any training triple shows its forward edit, its undo, and the DINOv3 similarity that let it through.
train_what: LoRA (r=32) on FLUX.2 Klein 4B in edit mode (reference-image conditioning) via mflux, trained on (source, Korean instruction, target) triples. Plus the engine's own components adapted: a LoRA on CapRL-Qwen3VL-2B to write Korean edit instructions in your phrasing, and UnifiedReward-Flex as the gate judge (prompt-following score ≥ 4/5).
data_plan: Own photos: 300 of your desk, plants, kitchen, city walks. Instruction generator: CapRL-2B lists 6 editable objects per photo → 1,200 instructions (add/remove/recolor/move/material), in Korean, from templates you wrote + 40 hand examples. Teacher: Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 Lightning 4-step at 768px produces forward edit, then the auto-inverted instruction ('다시 원래대로') produces the undo. Gates: DINOv3 cosine(source, undo) > 0.92; UnifiedReward judge ≥ 4; near-dup removal. Expect ~55% survival → ~650 clean triples; second round seeded from survivors to reach ~1,000. Held-out: 60 triples + 60 instructions you judge blind (teacher vs. student).
mac_plan: Teacher edits: 2,400 × ~15 s at 768px ≈ 10 h unattended (mflux 4-bit, ~14 GB). Gates: minutes. CapRL-2B LoRA for instruction style: 30 min in mlx-vlm. Klein 4B edit LoRA in mflux at 768px, 1k triples × 4 epochs ≈ 3 h (peak ~30 GB). Total ≈ 1 weekend of wall clock, ~2 h of attention.
demo: Dashboard page (gate funnel, pass rates per edit type, similarity histograms) + the interactive editor demo (student vs. teacher, Korean input) recorded as video and run live from the Mac for guests; dataset + LoRA published on HF with the engine code.
risk: Klein 4B edit-mode LoRA training in mflux is newer than its text-to-image path — verify the trainer accepts reference images before generating 10 h of data. Cycle-consistency admits edits that were no-ops (identity edits pass trivially) — add a minimum change threshold on the forward edit.
